title: GMAT Focus Quant Practice Test 23
instructions: GMAT Focus Edition Quantitative Reasoning: 21 Problem Solving questions, 45 minutes. An on-screen calculator is permitted.

questions.prompt: By what percentage does 84 exceed 60?
questions.explanation: 84 is 24 more than 60, and 24 out of 60 is 40%. Measuring the same gap against 84 gives 28.57%, which answers how much smaller 60 is than 84 — a different question with a different base.

questions.prompt: If 2 to the power a equals 32, what is a³?
questions.explanation: 2⁵ is 32, so a is 5. Cubing that gives 5³ = 125. 5 is the index itself, and 32 is what 2 raised to it comes to — neither is what the question asks for.

questions.prompt: How many of these seven readings are above their mean: 12, 15, 19, 22, 28, 34, 41?
questions.explanation: The seven total 171, so the mean is 24.43. Above it: 28, 34, 41 — 3 readings. The mean does not split a set in half: here 4 readings sit below it and only 3 above, because the largest values are spread further from the middle than the smallest.

questions.prompt: Taking pi as 22/7, a sector of a circle of radius 7 cm has an area of 77 cm². What is its angle at the centre?
questions.explanation: The whole circle has an area of 22/7 × 7² = 154 cm², so the sector is 77/154 of it — exactly half. Half of 360 degrees is 180 degrees. Reading the fraction as a percentage rather than scaling 360 by it gives 50 degrees.

questions.prompt: 30 kg of a mix is 2 parts salt to 3 parts sand, and 20 kg of another is 3 parts salt to 1 parts sand. The two are combined. What is the ratio of salt to sand in the result?
questions.explanation: The first lot holds 12 kg of salt and the second 15 kg, giving 27 kg of salt in 50 kg of mixture, so 23 kg is sand: 27 : 23. Adding the parts of the two ratios gives 5 : 4 and ignores that the lots are different sizes.

questions.prompt: What is the sum of the first 6 terms of 3, 6, 12, each term twice the one before?
questions.explanation: The six terms are 3, 6, 12, 24, 48, 96, which add to 189. The formula gives the same: 3 × (2⁶ − 1) / (2 − 1) = 3 × 63 = 189. 96 is the last term on its own.

questions.prompt: A game costs £2.00 to play and pays £5.00 with probability 0.3. What is the expected result per game?
questions.explanation: The expected winnings are £5.00 × 0.3 = £1.50 a game, against a stake of £2.00, so on average each game loses £0.50. £1.50 is what the game pays out on average before the stake is taken into account.

questions.prompt: 24 items in a batch of 3,000 are faulty. What is the fault rate in parts per thousand?
questions.explanation: 24 out of 3,000 is 24/3,000, and multiplying by 1,000 gives 8 per thousand. As a percentage the same rate is 0.8%, which is the figure to be careful of: parts per thousand runs ten times larger than a percentage.

questions.prompt: Three taps can fill a tank in 12, 15, 20 hours respectively. How long do all three take together?
questions.explanation: Their rates add: 1/12 + 1/15 + 1/20 = 5/60 + 4/60 + 3/60 = 12/60, or a fifth of the tank an hour. So together they take 5 hours. Averaging the three times gives 15.67 hours, longer than the fastest tap manages on its own.

questions.prompt: Taking pi as 22/7, what is the perimeter of a semicircle of radius 14 cm?
questions.explanation: The curved edge is half the circumference: 22/7 × 14 = 44 cm. The straight edge is the diameter, 28 cm, giving 72 cm in all. 44 cm leaves out the diameter, which a semicircle needs to be a closed shape.

questions.prompt: A number has 7 added to it, and the result is multiplied by 3 to give 45. What was the number?
questions.explanation: Undoing the steps in reverse: 45 divided by 3 is 15, and taking away 7 leaves 8. Checking forwards: 8 + 7 = 15, and 15 × 3 = 45. Stopping at 15 misses the last step, and taking 7 off 45 first gives 38, which undoes the operations in the order they were applied rather than in reverse.

questions.prompt: How long is it from 10:35 to 14:20?
questions.explanation: From 10:35 to 14:35 would be four hours, and 14:20 is 40 minutes short of that, so the answer is 3 hours 45 minutes. Subtracting the digits as though they were decimals gives 3 hours 85 minutes, which then has to be carried into 3 hours 45 minutes anyway.

questions.prompt: A car uses 8 litres of fuel per 100 km. How many kilometres does it travel on one litre?
questions.explanation: 8 litres carry the car 100 km, so one litre carries it 100 / 8 = 12.5 km. The two figures are reciprocals of each other: a car using fewer litres per 100 km travels further on each one, so a smaller consumption figure means a larger distance figure.

questions.prompt: Ten numbers have a mean of 40. One of them is increased by 30 and the others are unchanged. By what percentage does the mean rise?
questions.explanation: The total rises by 30, which spread over 10 numbers lifts the mean by 3. Against a mean of 40 that is 7.5%. Measuring the 30 against the mean directly gives 75% and forgets that the rise is shared between all 10 numbers.

questions.prompt: What is the median of the first 50 positive whole numbers?
questions.explanation: With 50 numbers in order the median sits between the 25th and the 26th, which are 25 and 26: their average is 25.5. An even-sized set has no single middle value, so the median need not be a whole number even when every value is.

questions.prompt: The interior angles of a polygon add to 1,440 degrees. How many sides does it have?
questions.explanation: The interior angles of an n-sided polygon add to (n − 2) × 180 degrees. Setting that equal to 1,440 gives n − 2 = 8, so n = 10. 8 is n − 2 rather than n — the 2 has to be added back.

questions.prompt: 3 machines print 4,500 pages in 15 minutes. At the same rate, how many pages do 5 machines print in 24 minutes?
questions.explanation: 3 machines over 15 minutes is 45 machine-minutes for 4,500 pages, so one machine-minute prints 100. 5 machines over 24 minutes is 120 machine-minutes: 12,000 pages. Scaling by the machines alone gives 7,500.

questions.prompt: The roots of x² − 7x + 12 = 0 are p and q. What is 1/p + 1/q?
questions.explanation: 1/p + 1/q is (p + q) / pq. For x² − 7x + 12, the roots add to 7 and multiply to 12, so the answer is 7/12. The roots themselves are 3 and 4, and 1/3 + 1/4 is indeed 7/12 — but the coefficients give it without solving anything.

questions.prompt: Our price is £96.00 and a competitor charges £72.00. What percentage discount would bring our price down to theirs?
questions.explanation: The gap is £24.00, and a discount is measured against our own price: £24.00 / £96.00 = 25%. Measuring it against the competitor's price gives 33.33%, which is how much dearer we are than them rather than how much we must come down.

questions.prompt: If f(x) = 3x − 2 and g(x) = x², what is f(g(4))?
questions.explanation: Work from the inside out: g(4) is 4² = 16, and f(16) is 3 × 16 − 2 = 46. Applying the functions the other way round, as g(f(4)), gives 100 — composition is not commutative, so the order matters.

questions.prompt: £12,000.00 is split between an account paying 4% and one paying 7%, earning £690.00 in a year altogether. How much is in the 7% account?
questions.explanation: All £12,000.00 at 7% would earn £840.00, which is £150.00 too much. Every pound moved to the 4% account gives up 3p a year, so £5,000.00 sits there and £7,000.00 at 7%. Checking: £200.00 plus £490.00 is £690.00.
